Terms and conditions

Pricing and payment
  1. Desired Prices. The prices entered in the brief are desired prices. They are not a commitment by the client or by WOOP. Final pricing is agreed with WOOP in writing before go-live.
  2. Project-Specific Pricing. The rates in this proposal apply only to this project. WOOP has the right to change them after the project is completed.
  3. Change in Costs. WOOP reserves the right to change the per-unit rate during the project if there is an unforeseen increase in social media advertising costs, a better understanding of the client’s campaign funnel, or unexpected rising overhead costs. Any increase will be made with at least 1 month’s notice. The client has the option to withdraw or stop the campaign if the new pricing is not sustainable.
  4. Billing Basis. WOOP charges only for completed actions, as measured by the agreed source of truth.
  5. Currency and Taxes. Invoices are raised in the currency in which pricing is negotiated. Tax on the total invoice value is additional, based on the tax regulations of the country of operation.
  6. Invoice Cycle. Invoice every 15 days, or once a base threshold revenue of SGD 2,000 is met, whichever is earlier.
  7. Payment Period. Invoices are payable within 60 days of invoice date.
  8. Late Payment Interest. Interest of 8% per annum may be charged from the day of default.
  9. Pause on Overdue. WOOP may pause the program and stop sending data and reports if any payment is overdue by more than 30 days.
  10. Discontinuation. If the client discontinues the project after it has started, for reasons outside WOOP’s control, the client pays for the work delivered to date.
Budget, duration and delivery
  1. Budget and Duration. The client may set a budget cap, a duration, both, or neither. WOOP will not spend beyond a budget cap, and will not run beyond a duration, that the client has set.
  2. No Guarantee of Volume. WOOP does not guarantee that the number of completed actions the client asks for will be reached. WOOP will keep the campaign active for as long as needed to get as close to it as possible, within any budget cap or duration the client has set.
  3. Ramp-Up and Pilot Optimisation. The start is typically slow as WOOP learns, and optimisations begin after the learnings. Delivery per day may be slower in the first few weeks. During pilot phases, WOOP takes time to optimise quality, so early quantity may be lower and success is measured on the latest batch delivered.
  4. Scale Estimates. Volume forecasts are estimates and depend on audience profile, geography and client-side conversion. Higher scale can be delivered at a higher cost per action.
  5. Working Days and Holidays. All WOOP operations run from India. Holidays relevant to India, plus holidays in the client’s country of operation, will affect the project timeline. WOOP will keep the client informed of these potential days.
  6. Client Delays. Any delay caused by the client will delay the go-live date. WOOP is not responsible for hitting KPI numbers within the agreed duration if launch is delayed for reasons outside WOOP’s control.
  7. Client Feedback. To optimise efficiently, WOOP requests the client to provide detailed feedback on quality on a weekly basis.
How WOOP works
  1. Not Exclusive. WOOP is not exclusive to any brand. WOOP works with brands from competing categories, and may run campaigns for competitors at the same time, including in the client’s category.
  2. Platform, Not Agency. WOOP is a platform that works with multiple clients in the industry, many of them in the same category. WOOP does not create assets for the brand. All content needs to be provided by the client.
  3. Medium and Channel. To drive the agreed action or outcome, WOOP will operate within the WOOP ecosystem. The choice of medium and channel lies with WOOP.
  4. Consumer Journey. WOOP has multiple brands on its platform, but a brand’s journey is dedicated to that brand alone. The consumer journey before and after the brand journey is not open to client edits or approvals. The client’s own journey can be approved and controlled by the brand within what is possible. WOOP is not compelled to share details of competitive brands present on WOOP now or added in future. The choice of which brand to interact with lies with the consumer.
  5. Journey Changes. WOOP may change the order of steps or screens in the consumer journey to optimise funnel results. Changes in content, copy or images that affect the brand’s communication or equity will be checked with the client before optimisation. If the number of actions or steps increases after the journey structure is approved, the launch may be delayed, impacting KPI performance within the agreed time frame.
Actions and how they are measured
  1. Definition of an Action. The brief names the exact actions being delivered, along with the geography and the audience profile.
  2. Source of Truth and Tracking. Completed actions are measured via client analytics, pixel, postback or WOOP tracking, as agreed. The client will implement and test tracking before go-live and share action tracking with WOOP regularly and transparently. Google Analytics access is preferred. If tracking breaks on the client’s side, WOOP is not responsible for the resulting reporting gap.
  3. Reporting Differences. Differences of up to 10% between WOOP’s and the client’s numbers are accepted. Beyond this, both parties will reconcile in good faith.
  4. Client Asset Readiness. The client’s destination must be live, functional, mobile-ready and stable throughout the campaign. Downtime or broken flows that reduce actions do not count against WOOP’s KPI.
  5. Changes at the Destination. Any change to the steps to complete the action, or to the offer, price or stock, must be shared with WOOP in advance. Such changes may or may not impact KPI delivery and pricing.
  6. Invalid Actions. Invalid actions include bots, duplicates, off-geography and off-profile actions. The client must raise disputes with supporting evidence within 10 days of receiving a report. Valid disputes will be credited or replaced. After this window, reports are deemed accepted.
  7. No Guarantee Beyond the Action. WOOP delivers the defined action from the agreed audience profile. WOOP does not guarantee downstream outcomes such as sales, revenue or retention. Narrower profiling increases cost per action and reduces scale.
  8. No Data Handling. WOOP does not collect or receive consumer personal data in Actions campaigns. Any data captured on the client’s assets belongs to the client, who is responsible for consent, its privacy policy and legal compliance. If personal data transfer is added to a proposal, the data terms below apply.
If you choose Get a lead: data terms
  1. Permitted Use. Leads may be used to retarget via social media audiences, emailers, SMS, WhatsApp, phone calls, and courier of samples or other promotional material.
  2. No Third-Party Sharing. The client cannot share leads with any third party without taking the consumer’s consent again.
  3. Data Breach. As per GDPR guidelines, if a data breach happens for any unforeseen reason, WOOP will inform the client at the earliest, and any data transferred to the client as a result of the breach must be deleted at the client’s end. WOOP will not compensate the client or any third party for any data loss.
  4. Client Data Security. WOOP is not responsible for any leakage of consumer information that happens at the client’s end. The client takes full responsibility for the security of the consumer data it collects from WOOP.
  5. Opt-In Validity. Consumer opt-in is valid for 3 years from the timestamp of the opt-in, or for as long as validity is allowed in the country of operation.
  6. Privacy Policy. WOOP is not responsible for the choice of words used by the client in its privacy policy or legal opt-in clause.
  7. Data Ownership. Data ownership lies with both WOOP and the client. Data is first collected for WOOP with a WOOP legal opt-in. A secondary opt-in is then taken, asking for consent to pass the data to the client. WOOP is not liable to delete consumer data it already owns before consent to share with the client is taken.
  8. Sensitive Information. No sensitive information is collected on behalf of any client.
  9. Data Transfer. WOOP prefers API integration with clients for data transfer, as it improves the consumer experience and engagement rates.
  10. Questions and Engagement Content. Unless otherwise specified, all education, engagement, insight or data-attribute questions are multiple-choice, close-ended with a single-click answer. Engagement content can be an image, text, infographic or a 15-20 second video.
Pilot and commitment
  1. Post-Pilot Proposal. Upon completion of the pilot, WOOP will present a proposal outlining the pricing and scale required to continue actions on an ongoing basis. Pilot rates may not be sustained at scale, and scale-up pricing is agreed after the pilot.
  2. Feedback Frequency. Feedback on quality is needed much more frequently in the pilot, as WOOP is learning to optimise run-rate and quality. In scale-ups the frequency can come down.
  3. Pilot Duration. The timeline may vary depending on the performance of the campaign. Once WOOP has its learnings, it will confirm the duration needed to complete the campaign.
  4. Intent to Invest. After the first engagement with WOOP, if the client is happy with the quality of the results, the client is open to investing at least the equivalent of Rs. 300,000 (in the currency the client chose) with WOOP over the next 12 months for the stated actions. This is a minimum.
